content: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction necessitates avoiding the combination or using an alternative drug. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases clarithromycin levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of resmetirom through other mechanisms. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Resmetirom, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, should not be coadministered with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Both ribociclib and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of vonoprazan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of vonoprazan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of vonoprazan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. While clarithromycin is a strong CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibitor, pharmacokinetic data suggest no precautions are necessary in patients with normal renal function. However, avoid the combination in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment (CrCl 15–80 mL/min). Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided if possible. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, increasing the risk of myopathy. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg BID in patients with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid use in patients with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage. After discontinuation of the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous selumetinib dose. Clarithromycin and sertraline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin and sevoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Increased systemic exposure to phosphodiesterase inhibitors may occur with clarithromycin; consider reducing the dosage of these inhibitors. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Both clarithromycin and siponimod prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and solifenacin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should not be coadministered with sonidegib. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin and sotalol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of vonoprazan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of vonoprazan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration upon resumption. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase abemaciclib to the pre-inhibition dose. Clarithromycin and albuterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and alfuzosin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Vonoprazan increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors does not require initial dosage modification, but dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin and arformoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg PO daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Clarithromycin and azithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates cannot be avoided, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive substrate. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Decrease the betrixaban dose to 80 mg PO once, then 40 mg PO daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bosentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for adverse reactions. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also coadministered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for signs of overmedication. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should be transitioned to a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine long-acting injection by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for signs of toxicity or overdose. If necessary, transition the patient back to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of calcifediol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP450 inhibitors may alter vitamin D metabolism, potentially affecting serum calcifediol levels and its conversion to calcitriol. Dose adjustment of calcifediol may be required. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
